coverage.main: Read all 34 pages of arXiv 2310.08419v4 (last updated 18 July 2024; the unversioned arXiv PDF resolved to identical bytes on the review date), including Sections 1-6, Tables 1-7, Figures 1-6, and Appendices A-H. Transfer and defense results checked on PDF pp. 6-8 (Table 3, Sections 4.2-4.3, Table 5).
coverage.supplement: Appendices A-H are embedded in the arXiv PDF and were read: Table 8 (AdvBench direct attacks), attacker generation details, judge prompts, system prompts and generation examples. No separate supplement is linked. The corpus DOI resolves to IEEE Xplore document 10992337 (SaTML 2025), which was not accessible without a subscription through the review tools; the version of record is therefore not claimed inspected, and any differences from arXiv v4 remain unchecked.
coverage.excluded_results: Table 2, Table 8 and Figure 4 are direct query attacks on each target, not cross-model transfer. The attacker LLM generates prompts but is not a source model whose successful attacks are transferred. Table 1 compares judge functions; Table 4 is efficiency; Tables 6-7 and Figures 5-6 are attacker/system-prompt ablations with Vicuna as the directly attacked target. Appendix figures are qualitative examples. These are retained only as setup evidence (Table 2 supplies the source-success counts used by Table 3).

result_groups.population: PAIR prompts that jailbroke the source (GPT-4 or Vicuna) in the Section 4.1 direct-attack run on JBB-Behaviors
result_groups.outcome: Llama Guard judges the target response jailbroken
result_groups.evidence: Caption: percentage of prompts that successfully jailbreak a source LLM when transferred. Section 4.2: uses the successful jailbreaks found for GPT-4 and Vicuna. Arithmetic corroborates the restriction: GPT-4-source transfer to Vicuna is 71%, above GPT-4's own 48% direct JB% over 100 behaviors, impossible with a 100-behavior denominator. No target-clean-correct analog is defined for jailbreak judging, so field 2 is unclear, not no.

result_groups.population: GCG suffixes that jailbroke Vicuna at the final optimization step
result_groups.outcome: Llama Guard judges the target response jailbroken
result_groups.evidence: Section 4.2 states that, following Zou et al., successful jailbreaks found at the final optimization step for Vicuna are transferred. This is an explicit source-success restriction. Whether the final-step success set equals Table 2's 56% is not stated. The JailbreakBench GCG transfer files contain 100 prompts per target and do not match Table 3's GPT-3.5 cell, so the implementation population is flagged as unresolved; this does not override the explicit reporting.

result_groups.population: Prompts obtained by attacking the undefended LLM, passed to the same LLM wrapped by SmoothLLM or a perplexity filter; JB% over the 100 JBB behaviors
result_groups.outcome: Llama Guard judges the defended target response jailbroken
result_groups.evidence: Section 4.3 describes static evaluation: prompts are obtained against an undefended LLM and passed to a defended LLM. The undefended row reproduces Table 2. Whether prompts for behaviors without an undefended success are also passed is not stated; the defended values do not exceed undefended values, which is consistent with either policy. Treated as transfer from undefended to defended system; no target-clean analog is defined.

f1.evidence: The outcome is a judged jailbreak on harmful behaviors, not classification accuracy. The paper reports undefended direct JB% per model, but no clean-input baseline analogous to separate source/target clean accuracy is defined for this task. Recorded as a task-mapping limitation, not deficient reporting.

f2.evidence: All three groups are unclear because no target-clean-correct event exists for a jailbreak judge. Absence of image-classification clean filtering is not evidence of an explicit no.

f3.evidence: Both Table 3 groups explicitly restrict transfer to source-successful jailbreaks (any_explicit_yes = true); the static-defense Table 5 group does not state whether unsuccessful undefended prompts are passed. Paper-level unclear arises from that unresolved scope, not from missing conditioning in the headline transfer table.

f4.evidence: No literal counts are printed. JB% is defined over 100 behaviors, so Table 2 and Table 5 integer percentages give counts k/100. Table 3 PAIR denominators are the Section 4.1 successes (GPT-4 48, Vicuna 88); with nearest-unit rounding every PAIR cell has a unique numerator (e.g., 71% -> 34/48, 52% -> 46/88) via survey/count_reconstruction.py. The GCG row's final-step denominator is not stated to equal Table 2's 56; if it did, cells would be unique (57% -> 32/56), but that identity is an assumption. Kept unclear.

f5.evidence: The attack is defined as finding any prompt P such that the judge flags the response (Eq. 2), with no norm constraint; PAIR rewrites whole semantic prompts and GCG optimizes discrete suffix tokens. No L-infinity or L2 radius applies. This is an explicit methodological property of a text jailbreak task, not an omission of a budget the paper should have reported; report it in the non-image applicability stratum.

f6.locator: Section 4 Target LLMs (p. 6); Appendix H (p. 34); artifact_checks below
f6.evidence: PAIR code is public (MIT) and JailbreakBench hosts per-behavior PAIR/GCG prompts and responses. But the hosted PAIR direct-attack counts (e.g., Vicuna 82/100 under jailbroken_llama_guard1, 69/100 under jailbroken; GPT-3.5 76 or 71) do not match Table 2 (88, 51), no PAIR transfer outcomes are hosted, and GCG transfer files cover 100 prompts rather than an identified source-success subset. Closed targets are dated hosted API versions whose continued availability and determinism were not verified. No sufficient per-example record for Table 3 is established; not a claim that the paper is irreproducible.

artifact_checks.result: Cloned and pinned. Contains PAIR attack/judge/model wrappers, a 50-behavior AdvBench subset and Docker setup. README recommends 20 streams and documents older judge options, whereas the paper uses N=30, K=3 and Llama Guard via JailbreakBench. No transfer script, published outputs or logs are tracked. Not executed (requires paid hosted APIs and local 13B/7B weights).

Cloned and pinned. PAIR black_box files (evaluation date 2024-03-06, N=30, K=3, Mixtral attacker) exist for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-2 and Vicuna only; counts do not reproduce Table 2 under either judge field. GCG transfer files (2024-03-18) hold 100 Vicuna-derived prompts per GPT target with 47/100 and 4/100 jailbroken (34 and 1 under the Llama Guard 1 field), not an identified source-success subset. No Claude or Gemini artifacts. Treated as related benchmark artifacts, not the Table 3 records.
Resolves to https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10992337/; full text not accessible through the review tools. Version-of-record differences not inspected.

bounds_checks.reason: Judged jailbreak is not a fixed-predictor misclassification probability, no clean-error baseline event is defined, and the rates are conditioned on source success. The classification bound max(0, rate - clean error) is not applicable.
Jailbreak outcome under defenses; no matched clean baseline. Not substituted into the misclassification identity.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit; supersedes the metric-level rank-1 note in batch_01_06_10.md, whose Table 3 source-success finding is retained and corroborated arithmetically.
The SaTML version of record was not accessible; judgments rest on arXiv v4 and its embedded appendices.

Count reconstruction assumes one prompt per successful behavior and nearest-unit rounding; the GCG denominator identity is unresolved. No runtime or hosted-API recomputation attempted; no numerical bound is computed.
